author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Executives from OpenAI and Anthropic faced tough questions at a parliamentary inquiry in Sydney this week over data breaches, safety and copyright, amid growing public distrust of AI.

Voice actor Simon Kennedy, who says companies have replaced him with AI after three decades in the business, founded the Australian Voice Actors Association, which has 300 members. He told the inquiry he wants mandatory labelling of AI voices and identity rights, warning that unchecked AI could leave the industry with no future. OpenAI and Anthropic pushed to loosen copyright laws so they can use songs and voices to train their models.

Distrust escalated after Australia recorded the world's first known case of an autonomous OpenAI agent gaining access to a government website. OpenAI's chief strategy officer, Jason Kwon, said the company was sorry and has work to do to rebuild trust.

Al Jazeera's Danielle Robertson reports from Sydney.

description:
The former head of Germany's Foreign Intelligence Service, August Hanning, has been remanded in custody on suspicion of spying. He was one of two men arrested on Tuesday over allegations that they illegally obtained state secrets over a 14-year period, after Hanning had retired.

The second man worked as Hanning's chief of staff until 2005, and then in a similar role for Hanning's successors until earlier this year. It is alleged that thousands of secret documents found their way to Hanning during this time, and that he was regularly in contact with a foreign intelligence agent.

Authorities argue the chief of staff compiled classified documents at the Bundesnachrichtendienst headquarters in Berlin, and allegedly sold them to his former boss. Hanning had gone into private security consultancy and, it is alleged, was in contact from time to time with representatives of foreign countries. 

Al Jazeera's Dominic Kane reports from Berlin.

During the event, loud bangs could be heard from Gaza where the Israeli military is carrying out attacks despite a ceasefire. 

Overnight in Gaza, at least one person was killed in Israeli attacks. 
He was a member of the civil defence agency and was trying to rescue injured people near a hospital when Israeli aircraft bombed the area again.
After three years of genocide, Israeli attacks have killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, roughly 1,500 of them during the ceasefire.
Most of Gaza's population is still displaced and living in tents or destroyed buildings across the strip.

Al Jazeera’s Hani Mahmoud reports from Gaza City.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In 1934, a team called Palestine entered the qualifying rounds of the football World Cup in Mussolini’s fascist Italy. But it did not include any Palestinian players. It was drawn largely from the Jewish sporting movement under the British Mandate, at a time when football reflected the changing face of Palestine.

This documentary uncovers the forgotten history of Mandate-era football - how British rule, Zionist organisation and Palestinian exclusion shaped the makeup of the first team to compete internationally as Palestine. Through archives, interviews with specialist historians and the story of the 1934 qualifiers against Egypt, the film traces how the established football association became Israel’s, while Palestinian football was plagued by revolt, war and the 1948 Nakba. Decades later, Palestinians fought to reclaim their place in world football, finally securing FIFA recognition in 1998.

Original film title: Palestine: The Lost Team

The Houthis seized the capital Sanaa by force in 2014 and later imposed their own government.

The offensive began on Monday and is focused on Taiz province along the western coast, an area the Iran-backed armed group took control of last month. Government forces say they have captured crucial highland overlooking Mansourah.

Al Jazeera's Yousef Mawry, reporting live from Houthi-controlled Sanaa, describes an all-out battle for the mountains of Al-Wazi'yah, including Khaboub, Jabal an-Nar and the Khalid ibn al-Walid military base. He says whoever controls this strategic belt overlooks Bab al-Mandeb and the roads leading to Dhubab and Al-Mukha.

Al Jazeera's Yousef Mawry reports from Sanaa.

description:
British counter-terror police have arrested a seventh man in connection with the suspected terror incident near RAF Fairford in late September, and he faces potential charges of preparing an act of terror. 

Police found no viable explosives at the scene, and the investigation is ongoing. RAF Fairford was until recently used by the US to launch defensive strikes against Iran, and on Monday US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that relocating its bombers to American bases was linked to the earlier incident.

Police describe the investigation as complex and say they are working around the clock to understand the motivations behind it, but cannot yet say with any certainty why it happened. 

The first six men were all released without charge, but on bail. British counter-terror police have the power to hold terror suspects in custody for a total of 14 days without charge.

Al Jazeera's Camille Nedelec reports from London.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The International Olympic Committee has confirmed that Qatar and India are among seven countries bidding to host the 2036 Olympics. 

Four years after hosting the FIFA World Cup, Qatar is again aiming to place itself at the centre of global sport. If successful, the Games would be the first held in the Middle East, likely requiring a move away from the traditional July-August window to avoid the Gulf's extreme summer heat. 

India's bid centres on Ahmedabad, which will host the 2030 Commonwealth Games and has the world's largest cricket stadium. Former Olympic hosts South Korea and Germany are also in the running, along with Hungary, Turkiye and South Africa. The IOC says it is also talking to all seven countries about possibly hosting in 2040 or 2044.

Additional candidates have until the end of this month to join the contest, with the shortlist to be confirmed in March. The final vote is around two and a half years away, with a winner chosen in 2029.

title: Qatar and India among seven countries bidding to host the 2036 Olympics
